source: Inria PIRAT, A New Hope for DARPA OpTC (CSET 2025). corrected labels. UNION observed (non-summary) actions from our own ground truth.
unit: malicious process lifetime interval (host, pid, start, end)
why_intervals: a planted process keeps running, so every window it is alive in contains attack activity. Point labels on the action minute mark one window positive and the rest negative, which scores a correct detection as a false positive.
open_ended_note: rows whose end is 'Infinity': the process was still alive when the capture stopped. Clamped to the end of its own day or to the capture end, whichever is earlier. These are the longest lived malicious processes and therefore cover the most windows.
dropped_reason: no eCAR telemetry for this host; a full scan found 450 hosts and none of them DC1 (docs/19 section 3). Same exclusion as the previous label set.
union_note: a window is positive if a malicious process was alive in it (Inria) OR an observed operator action happened in it (ours). Summary lines with rounded times are excluded: they are real activity that cannot be placed in a window. This is the sensitivity set; the primary label set is the unmodified Inria one (ADR-0023).
